newsitem.title: UK: Quiet Eurobonds see Moldova make debut in dollars.
newsitem.headline: Quiet Eurobonds see Moldova make debut in dollars.

text.p: Moldova's debut Eurobond was the highlight of a quiet Friday morning in the primary market before the release of key U.S. jobs data and the weekend.
The other main events were the overnight launches of a NZ$500 million global bond for Fannie Mae and a $750 million FRN for Caisse Centrale du Credit Immobilier.
Moldova launched a $75 million five-year deal at a 340 basis points spread over U.S. Treasuries via Merrill Lynch. Final pricing was due later.
Moldova, rated Ba2 by Moody's, held a global roadshow for the offering in the second half of May.

Moldova's Ba2 sovereign ceiling took into account the relative success of stabilization efforts following the severe disruptions ensuing form the break-up of the Soviet Union, Moody's said in March in its first report on the country.
Moody's said the government had demonstrated a determination to manage its fiscal and monetary policies in a prudent manner.
"Evidence of a stabilized economy indicates that the macro policy framework is beginning to produce results," Moody's said.
Including $570 million owed to Russian gas monopoly Gazprom, Moldova's external debt totals $1.2 billion -- about 60 percent of gross domestic product.

Merrill Lynch helped Moldova make a $30 million private placement last year, the first time the former Soviet republic tapped international capital markets. The three-year deal carried an 11 percent coupon.

The five-year U.S. Treasury note was trading at 6.48 percent in London, meaning Moldova/Merrill could opt for a 10 percent coupon on today's deal as well, double digits being a rarity and thus popular with retail investors.
Merrill Lynch was unwilling to comment on the deal before the final pricing, due to U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission regulations.
Elsewhere, Fannie Mae launched a NZ$500 million five-year global bond which will be priced later to yield 20-22 b.p. over N.Z. government paper.
Neither of the joint lead managers, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and Toronto-Dominion, was immediately available for comment.
